answer: An exit burn makes washing identities ruinous. A new identity stakes 200 credits; leaving burns 100, and re-entry restarts 12 tundra epochs of frozen zero-weight maturation. An island identity cannot hide this history: exits and re-entries are posted on a ledger auditors check before granting weight. A garden of identities costs capital each time: the kth fake stakes 200 and burns 100 on exit, so 1,000 fakes lock 200,000 and lose 100,000 on the first wash, about 3 percent left after five. Rented history fails as it is bound to one key and resets on transfer. One honest agent stakes once.
